title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
slides: Who loses when websites slam doors on AI agents?
Publishers now detect and block automated scraping in real time
But blocking agents also breaks accessibility tools and search
Your integrations may silently fail without warning
Test one blocked page today and log the failure
thread_text:
1. Your AI tools might be silently blocked

Publishers are now detecting and blocking automated scraping in real time, often without warning. Your integrations could stop working overnight.

2. Blocking agents breaks accessibility too

Screen readers and search engines often rely on the same automated requests that publishers are blocking. Real users get caught in the crossfire.

3. Silent failures are the worst kind

Your AI agent might return empty results or partial data, and you won't know until someone reports a problem. No error, no alert.

4. The web is fragmenting fast

As more sites block AI agents, the open web becomes less open. Integrations that worked yesterday may fail tomorrow, and you won't see it coming.

5. Test one blocked page today

Pick a page your AI relies on, try to fetch it, and log the failure. If you haven't done it, start there before your users notice.
